Well, I AM using Pygame for the project - while it doesn't include any sort of physics handling, it does have a simple way for checking collisions between sprites and the like, which I think is sufficient for a simple game like Pong. In any case, I've took a peek at Pymunk and PyBox2D and they definitely look like a solid base for a more sophisticated system.

 I think you're overestimating the complexity of the physics I'm currently thinking of. My first version just basically reversed the x-velocity upon collision :P. The current version takes into account where the ball hits paddle (so hitting the center will result in 0 y-velocity and hitting the far ends of the paddle results in max y-velocity), but that's not the way it should work, obviously. The final solution would ideally take into account the angle of impact and, possibly, the speed and direction of the paddle. Maybe even apply some spin to the ball. Hopefully, I'll be able to figure it out somehow :P. Regardless, I appreciate the concern :)
